dataset: Digital Science–Make Data Count Open Data Citations, release 202610

papers.title: Data reuse and the open data citation advantage
papers.reading_depth: Full text: methods, reuse operationalization, results and limitations inspected.
papers.contribution: Analyzes 10,555 gene-expression studies; distinguishes article citation advantage from accession-attributed third-party reuse. Adjusted citation association is about 9%. Authors inspect citation contexts and identify reuse through GEO/ArrayExpress accessions and depositor/citing-author surname overlap.
papers.dataset_relevance: The closest methodological precedent for mixed DOI/accession corpus links and for separating investigator reuse from third-party reuse.
papers.research_question: Among links labelled Secondary, what fraction actually describe third-party analysis rather than mere mention, and how do accession and DOI records differ?
papers.design_and_limits: Count distinct publication–dataset edges by dataset_id_type and repository; validate a stratified sample using article contexts. Author overlap and time-to-reuse require author/date metadata enrichment. Surname overlap is imperfect; do not equate Secondary with third-party reuse.

papers.title: Bringing Citations and Usage Metrics Together to Make Data Count
papers.reading_depth: Publisher full text: conceptual framing, Scholix, COUNTER and limitations inspected.
papers.contribution: Explains how Scholix article–data links and standardized COUNTER data usage metrics can be exposed together. It treats citation and usage as complementary dimensions; views/investigations and downloads/requests require defined counting rules.
papers.dataset_relevance: Direct intellectual foundation for Make Data Count. The released six-column corpus provides publication–dataset links, not standardized views/downloads.
papers.research_question: How much do repository-level interpretations of data impact change when citation indicators are compared with standardized usage indicators?
papers.design_and_limits: Corpus can supply link counts and Secondary shares by repository. Answering the comparison requires separately available, compatible usage reports; downloads still do not prove scientific reuse.

papers.title: Measuring the Value of Research Data: A Citation Analysis of Oceanographic Data Sets
papers.reading_depth: Full text: search/counting methods, findings and interpretation inspected.
papers.contribution: Attempts to count citations and mentions to three curated oceanographic datasets using Web of Science, publisher full-text search and Google Scholar. Finds inconsistent citation forms despite recommended formats and demonstrates the importance of multiple detection routes.
papers.dataset_relevance: Supports a measurement audit of DOI-only versus accession-inclusive indicators and warns that counts depend on search coverage and what counts as a citation.
papers.research_question: How sensitive are apparent dataset and repository impact rankings to identifier type, mention detection and duplicate counting?
papers.design_and_limits: Compare publication counts, distinct identifier counts and distinct edges by dataset_id_type/repository; trace selected source articles where available. Entity merging requires verified aliases; do not assume several accessions represent several independent datasets.

papers.title: An examination of research data sharing and re-use: implications for data citation practice
papers.reading_depth: Publisher abstract and bibliographic metadata only; subscription full text not accessed.
papers.contribution: Examines Genetics and Heredity citation practices using the Data Citation Index and 148 sampled citing articles. Its citer-based approach considers formal and implicit citations, self-citation, main text, supplements, acknowledgments and author information.
papers.dataset_relevance: Provides a concrete precedent for validation using citing articles rather than trusting index-level citation counts.
papers.research_question: Does the meaning and accuracy of a Secondary label vary by repository, identifier system and citation location?
papers.design_and_limits: Draw a stratified sample using repository, dataset_id_type and citation_type; inspect source context and independently annotate actual reuse. The paper abstract supports the design, not unverified numerical outcomes or a claim of classifier accuracy.

papers.title: Analyzing data citation practices using the data citation index
papers.venue: Journal of the Association for Information Science and Technology
papers.reading_depth: Crossref abstract plus openly available author manuscript: methods, repository coverage and discussion inspected.
papers.contribution: Analyzes Data Citation Index records by field, object type and repository. Reports that 88.1% of records in its historical DCI sample were uncited, with substantial variation across repositories and disciplines.
papers.dataset_relevance: Shows how infrastructure coverage and repository/object conventions shape measured citation activity. Its uncitedness result cannot be transferred to a corpus containing observed citation edges.
papers.research_question: Which apparent cross-repository differences persist after separating object types and accounting for index coverage?
papers.design_and_limits: Use repository and dataset_id_type to describe observed edges; attach verified dataset/object metadata for stratified comparisons. Uncitedness and reuse rates need a separate inventory of all eligible datasets, including those absent from the corpus.

papers.title: Theory and practice of data citation
papers.venue: Journal of the Association for Information Science and Technology
papers.reading_depth: Crossref abstract plus openly available accepted manuscript: identification, granularity and provenance sections inspected.
papers.contribution: Synthesizes the purposes and technical problems of data citation, including identification, attribution, fixity, provenance, variable granularity, versions and dynamic datasets. Persistent identifiers alone do not solve subset/version identification.
papers.dataset_relevance: Explains why dataset_id is an identifier unit rather than automatically an independent conceptual dataset, and why accession/DOI comparisons need entity-resolution rules.
papers.research_question: How much do impact concentration and repository rankings change when records are counted as identifiers, versions, dataset families or collections?
papers.design_and_limits: Start from (dataset_id_type, repository, dataset_id) as a cautious provisional key; enrich with verified parent/version/alias relations before aggregation. Publish sensitivity analyses rather than silently collapsing distinct entities.

papers.title: On the Reuse of Scientific Data
papers.reading_depth: Publisher full text: conceptual framework and research questions inspected.
papers.contribution: Explains why making data available is different from achieving reuse, and why use/reuse boundaries depend on actors, purposes, provenance and scientific context. Proposes six research questions about reuse, reproducibility, integration and release practices.
papers.dataset_relevance: Provides construct validity for interpreting Primary/Secondary/Unclassified labels: a link or label is evidence about an article–data relationship, not a complete account of what researchers did.
papers.research_question: Which forms of reuse—replication, integration, novel analysis or method testing—are represented by Secondary links, and which are missed?
papers.design_and_limits: The six released columns cannot identify reuse purpose. Context-based manual coding, potentially assisted by trace information, can produce an explicit reuse taxonomy and measured agreement with corpus labels.

papers.title: Attitudes and norms affecting scientists’ data reuse
papers.reading_depth: Full text: behavioral model, measures, results and limitations inspected.
papers.contribution: Uses DataONE survey responses and the Theory of Reasoned Action to study self-reported reuse. Perceived efficacy, efficiency and importance are associated with reuse behavior; perceived distrust and norms against reuse were not major impediments in the tested model.
papers.dataset_relevance: Adds behavioral dimensions that citation records do not observe, preventing a study of scholarly links from being presented as a complete study of researcher motivations.
papers.research_question: Do the communities with high observed Secondary-link activity also report benefits and practices associated with reuse?
papers.design_and_limits: Corpus can motivate community selection only after field enrichment. Testing motivations needs a survey or interview component, subject to a separate study decision and any ethics requirements; repository identity is not a behavioral measure.

papers.title: Measuring the impact of biodiversity datasets: data reuse, citations and altmetrics
papers.reading_depth: Publisher abstract and bibliographic metadata only; subscription full text not accessed.
papers.contribution: Studies openly available metadata for 43,802 GBIF datasets and content-codes 100 randomly sampled citing articles. Finds varied background and foreground reuse, inconsistent citation practice when many subsets are used, and altmetric mentions that often point to associated articles rather than datasets.
papers.dataset_relevance: Provides a newer, directly relevant empirical template combining large-scale dataset metadata with a small interpretable context audit; explicitly addresses subset aggregation and proxy validity.
papers.research_question: Among GBIF or comparable repository links, which Secondary relationships reflect foreground analytical reuse, background use or software testing, and how does counting many subsets affect apparent impact?
papers.design_and_limits: Use repository to select a documented subgroup, then annotate a stratified sample and report both distinct publications and distinct dataset identifiers. The corpus has no altmetrics or article contexts; those require enrichment. Foreground/background is a separate taxonomy from Primary/Secondary and must not be mapped automatically.

papers.title: The citation advantage of linking publications to research data
papers.reading_depth: Full text: DAS categories, citation models, findings and limitations inspected.
papers.contribution: Analyzes 531,889 PLOS/BMC articles, categorizing data availability statements. Repository-linked statements are associated with up to 25.36% higher article citation impact under its models; the paper discusses selection, coverage and other limitations.
papers.dataset_relevance: A stronger-scale comparison for citation-advantage research, while preserving the distinction between data availability statements, article citations and dataset reuse.
papers.research_question: Are Secondary links associated with later article visibility beyond the presence of a repository-linked availability statement?
papers.design_and_limits: Requires DAS text/categories, article citation outcomes, publication-year and venue/field controls, and an eligible article denominator. Use observational language and consider reverse timing and selection; release is a corpus version, not article publication year.
